transcript.content: No. This all sounds funny. I've got- What's that one? Is that the wireless knob?
Desk op. I don't know what these do. Is your mic working?
Sorry, I've got a bit of a cold.
Um... Oh God, I had a big list of things to talk about as well.
Yeah. No. Rocket from the Crypt.
Which is appropriate, 'cause we've got a little Gravediggaz track to play later, haven't we?
It's one of my favourite tracks, Gervais, by the Gravediggaz, but it has got a bit of bad language.
Well, that's okay, 'cause you've played it to me a couple of times and I reckon I've got it off pat.
I'm gonna- I'm gonna be bleeping it out live.
You're gonna do a live bleep-out?
Yeah. I should say, you know we usually have a few beers and we get... throughout the show, and I get steadily drunk, which is unprofessional. This saved a bit of time. Turned up pissed.
Yeah. So that... [unclear]. I'll tell you what, um...
I'll be honest with you, Gervais, Um, you know, normally uh, if someone gets drunk, their, um, their speech begins to slur.
That's the beauty of being me.
Yeah, exactly. How drunk are you?
Um, I had a little bit of wine.
It's a lovely... I might get a little bit melancholy. What about the little baby kangaroos that have to crawl all up their mums? I help 'em. Got a fax here for you, Steve, actually.

It's from, uh, um, Becky. Um, she's listening to us, um, in bed. She's been a bit lazy. Um, she's been on holiday and, um, she wants me to dedicate a song to, uh... to dedicate it to stinky, ska– skanky Steve because he is an alien.
Um, and she's done a little picture of him, Slimy Steve. Isn't that lovely? And she wants me to play, uh, “Subterranean Homesick Alien” by Radiohead. Isn't that sweet?
So people, people do think of you.

And I got one from, uh, Laura, as, uh, usual. Says to Steve, “You still sound as stupid as ever, you asymmetrical, asexual, rabid, anaemic, flea-ridden deformity.” Aww. See, you have got people thinking of you. See?
Babybird, “If You'll Be Mine”... then I'll be yours. And, uh, Babybird was actually in this week with Claire.
Oh, Baby Bird, was he at XFM?
He's got a beak and funny little claws.
I know, it made me laugh. It was a...
He used to be an egg.
We're desperate men, Rick, if you've got to resort to that kind of gag.
I called him Baby Bird. He went, I've never been called that before, which is bizarre.
But the band are called Babybird.
Can you go and turn that down next door? When we're trying to do a show.
Yeah, it's Emma, it's just, it's not on.
That's... that's insane. I can hear, I can hear a throb from the other room.
Someone's got... This is insane, Gervais. It's like having... trying to host a radio show.
Yeah, and now now he's laughing. Yeah.
Well, anyway, we're going to play a um, a track that you've brought in.
It's a fantastic tune by the Gravediggaz, part of the Wu-Tang Clan Rap Collective. Right, it's from their album.
Not to be confused with the Wu-Tang Clan. That's a little shellfish.
Yeah, Yeah. It just swears a lot.
The track is beautiful. You've probably heard it on the dance floor, maybe in some indie club. “1-800 Suicide”. Now, I would stress, Rick, it has got a bit of bad language.
I know. I I, I mean, I've, I've listened to this twice, and I reckon I've got it off pat. I reckon I'm going to pull the fader down to just the right places and go, eh. Okay?
Right, You're going to sort of bleep it out.
Yeah. And if it goes wrong, so what? You know, that's real. People have a problem with swearing. I don't. Do you?
I mean, I'm, I'm doing it because it's rules. And, you know, we were...
You know, the great thing about... rap...
We want to stay on air because, you know, we take our job seriously.
And, um, you know, I think we're, we're... We're... Sorry, excuse my French. Bloody good DJs.
Well, I think you're absolutely right, Rick. Yeah. Let me shake your hand.
There we are. Yeah. A good shaking of a hand. There. Um... I love a bit of rap.
Was it? It's weird, that is.
Um, oh, “pardon my French”, people always say when they...

Excuse my French, but la plume de ma tante! Hey, come on. Language, language. Um, we'll be doing... learning a little bit of a foreign language later. I've brought in, um, Instant Yiddish by Fred, uh, Kogos. I've always wanted to learn Yiddish.

Yeah. Um... narishkeit, foolishness. Um, tsum glik, tsum shlimen. Yeah, for better, for worse. So I'll be... I'll teach you little useless phrases like that out of the old Instant Yiddish book. But first, what was this? Gravediggaz?
It's Gravediggaz, erm, they're keeping it real, they're keeping it raw, so there is a bit of bad language.
Yeah, of course I have. Erm, right, I'm gonna have a go at this then.
No, don't, shut up, right, I've gotta play this. Shut up then, don't put me off, I've gotta concentrate.
I think there's one coming, Rick.
[Ricky dips the volume and makes a buzzing sound over a word in the song.]
You're doing okay, but you're not out of the woods yet.
[Ricky buzzes over more words in the record.]
Oh, you're doing well. I don't think there's any more.
I don't think there's any more.
Well done, Rick. No, it's very good.
That's Gravediggaz, innit? What's that called?
I'm gonna buy it. I mean...
Can I get that actual mix with me going "eh" on it?
And that's for Steve Vox, who's listening in Reading. It's from Lee, to him. And Steve is the president of the Geeks, Nerds and Losers Society, the GNL. Lee's the vice president.
I got thrown out of that.
What embarrassing walking down the street with you.
It was Saturday night last night.
And I didn't get to I didn't get to sleep until six in the morning.
I don't know why you hang around with 'em.
At least I look after you. I sort of... people say to me, is Steve really as ugly as you say? I go, he's worse. Do you know what I mean? But that's... No, do you know what I mean, though?
I tell you, one day, right, it's just one of me at the moment, but one day there'll be a whole squadron. It'll be like Planet of the Apes.
Oh, my God, and you don't actually need anyone else to sort of like, breed, do you?
Exactly! We can just reproduce as we are. It'll be like Planet of the Apes, right?
Get your damn dirty tentacle off me.
Exactly. And there'll just be loads of me crawling around.
And they'll see, like, Bristol Temple Meads, and they'll go, oh, my God, they blew it up!
It's back in Bristol with all your... Oh, no.

There must be an organisation of volunteers or summat who, if it's like touch and go, if it's really serious, if you're like clinically depressed about it and you really can't get a woman... They don't want just people turning up who can get girls and saying, “Oh, I fancy...” You know.

But in your case, they speak to you, they see you, and I think, you know, there must be some sort of national health thing or probably where you can actually sleep with, um, I don't know, a voluntary worker.
Do you know what I mean, though?

Yeah, Yeah, I know, but there's people that, um, I don't know, volunteer for geriatric duty, you know, and they're exploding all over the place. They're covered in the stuff, right? Um, There's people that work on leper colonies, right, for, you know, for nothing.
There must be someone who will sleep with you out of sympathy. You don't want that. Of course you don't. You don't want that, do you?
Well, let's not be hasty, Rick. I mean, these people, I mean, especially if they need some sort of free publicity, you know, get a bit of, um, you know, sort of press and media attention.
I ought to sort of help to publicise their campaign, really.

There's probably an organisation that go, you know, when we go, they go off to, like, um, strange climes and go on to, like, leper islands and that, and they work with them. Um, Or they can sleep with you. Now, that's got to do the lepers some good, doesn't it?
Wouldn't that be terrible if that was the option, right? And suddenly, volunteers to leper colonies doubled.
Let 'em on the bus. “Sorry, there's no room on the bus.” But you're at the back there, going, “Well, um... well then, here we go.”
No, no, but I, no, I'm sorry, I, I, I signed up for the, for the lepers.
Um, licking their wounds. Well, sorry, but...
Oh dear. Oh, you know, I heard a song in the week, right? I've heard it before. It's by Ween. And it goes-
[Sings] Push the little daisies and make 'em come up!
And I don't know what it's called. 0171 580 2000. I don't know where to look.
[Sings] Push the little daisies and make 'em come up! It's like that. It is.
I've been going around singing that.
There's no song with that lyric in.
It's like that. It goes- [Sings] Push the little daisies and make 'em come up!
[Over Ricky] Shut up! Shut up! Shut up!
That's what my friends have been saying for the last four days.
God, you're really irritating me today.
Like, people will go around going, [sings] "If you'll be mine," ah, not too annoying. But, um, after about ten times you go, "Oh, can you sing something else?" But when you've heard-
[Sings] Push the little daisies and make 'em come up!
[Over Ricky] Shut up! Shut up now!
Okay, Wannadies, "You and Me Song." [Sings] Push the little daisies-
[The song continues. Near the end they sing along.]
It's great, as if she's gonna gag. I love that one.
Maybe we should play it again.
I'm not that mad about it.
She's not quite as irritating... As.

Who is? Um, uh, we were talking earlier about how hideous you, um, how you look, and you can't get a woman because you're quite nasty as well. And, um, Emma, our producer here, who thought, “Oh, this is not fair,” you know, 'cause you are... Steve is quite affectionate.

When you get to sort of know... like E.T. When you first watch E.T., you go, “Urgh!” And then by the end you think, “Aww.” Do you know what I mean? It sort of, like, gets that deeper. And she said, she went, “Do I remind you, Steve, what I said when I first met you?” And this is like her best, you know, stab at a compliment to make you feel better.
She said, you know, I thought, "You're really not that ugly."
So the assumption is I am ugly, it's just not as bad as you've made out.
Like, you know what I mean, yeah. And just like, no, don't be silly, you're really good, you're really not that ugly. Yeah. It was a good effort though, wasn't it?
You know, that was that was nice, Emma, that was really nice. It was a good effort, but it was it was, it was shallow and futile. It doesn't mean anything. Look at his little face. Oh, look.
Look at that fax over there. Look at that fax over there, right?
“To Ricky, Steve's skin problem close up”, which is actually, um, silicon carbide particles.

Someone's sent in a fax, right, and they've got this sort of hideous, kind of mutated, um, cells, whatever, and they've put on the fax, “To Rick, Steve's skin problem close up.” You've never said I've got a skin problem.
No, I haven't. You haven't got a skin problem.

It's almost translucent, his skin. It's very pale. It's like, you know those newborn fish when you can see all the heart, can't you? All the hearts! Well, in many fish. They've got one each. Lots of fish, lots of hearts.
Gervais, shut up. You're irritating me now and you're abusive and you're just winding me up.
No, I'm a little bit offended by it.
I know. You see, you should be. But what about this, this charity thing? There must be one. 0171 580 2000. Oh, that'd be fantastic.
That'd be great. You know, it'd be like, uh, one pound fix, you'd write on the little form.
And you could get friends and relatives to sponsor you.
Would that be per stroke or per shag?
I think it's for the whole thing.

It'll be a big event. You know those guys, um, I think it was a hoax, but they were gonna televise the first moment they lost their virginity. And so They were gonna broadcast it down the internet. Alright?
And they were gonna have sex on the internet, live, and everyone's gonna applaud and watch and pay for it. Maybe I could organise that as well, make a bit of money out of it.
Yeah, but think of the technology by then, though.

They'd just be able to think it, won't they, and, like, see you losing your virginity. And they'll all have big swollen heads. You might be good-looking in, like, the year 2090. You never know, 'cause it's all relative, innit?
You know, in Bristol, you're a good looking fellow, aren't you, in Bristol?
Yeah, I mean, yeah. Oh, this is Belle and Sebastian. Uh, The boy with the Arab strap.

This is for Jim Hobbs, who said, uh... no, um, who said, “Can we hear more about Jezoc?” And I'd better tell people now. I've had a lot of faxes about Jezoc. Jezoc is spelt J-E-Z-O-C. I made it up, that's how it's spelt.
Gervais, you'll tell us a bit more about Jezok, will you?
Oh, yeah, yeah, I've got a new, I've got a whole new storyline.
Before you carry on, um, 01715802000, I've got some, um, sponsorship forms, like, already printed up.
So just send... you know, give me a call, I can post one to you.
“I will sleep with Steve”, or “I will go and work in a leper Connolly.” Connolly? Billy! Yeah.
Oh, shut up. Play a record.
This Scottish bloke with a beard with his legs falling off.
Just play a record, you drunken sot.
Gets quieter and quieter, doesn't it?

A couple of phone calls. Rob phoned in and said, “Slap Steve for saying 0181 instead of 0171.” See, it's the singly most important thing, the number. It's 0171 580 2000. That's why you don't hear me mucking that up.
Do you know what I mean?
Um, “Pump Ricky with more wine and challenge him to quack over the Anti-Nowhere League, ‘So What’.” I don't know, I've... I've... What's that? I think that's it again.
No, shut up. Um, I had something to say then.
I can smell it on your breath.
I can smell it on your breath, for God's sake.

Don't, don't wind me up, man. Um, yeah, I've got this new storyline for Jezoc. Um, I want... want help with it. What it is, right, I think it starts off with this villain, right, and Jezoc brings him in, right, and, uh, he's murdered maybe, maybe a little kid or, you know, someone's husband.
And The woman's there and she's terrible. Well, you would be.

Jezoc's in there and she goes... he goes, “Don't, don't worry. Um, he's gonna... by the time he gets out, um, Steve'll have a girlfriend,” right? She goes, “Oh, right. Right, won't bring my boy back, will it?” “No, but you can have one of mine.”
Um, I've got loads or something, right? Anyway, um, it goes to... Goes to the court, all right? And he's only tampered with the jury, and he's a nasty piece of work.
Yeah. He walks free, and he sort of, like, winks at Jezok on the way out. Do you think Jezoc's gonna let it lie?
Jezoc's not gonna let that villain, uh, what, has he got a piece of evidence?

Well, no, he goes after him, shoots him anyway, because, you know, it's just redundant. It turns out the bloke didn't actually do it. But, you know, as Jezok says, better, you know, kill innocent people than let one, you know, guilty person go free.

Yeah. Yeah. And shoot first, ask questions later. You know, you don't want to be stitched up. He's got a reputation. Um, and then, uh, he gets off with a woman, and they have they have another kid, and, uh, it's alright.
Um, Jezoc just killed an innocent man. He's your superhero. He's your, you know, your heroic hard-boiled cop. He just killed an innocent man. I'm a little bit disappointed.
Oh, so he's got to be perfect, has he?
Well, I'm just a little bit disappointed.
Well, no. He can't be perfect. He's got things to do. We know, We know he's got problems. He drinks too much. He kills innocent people. You go out there every day. See a, see how you survive.
Do you know what I mean?
We got Mama Said Knock You Out lined up. It's uh, one of our joint little favourites. We like this one and we like some other songs, don't we?
Um, It's Jezoc, right? And he retires. He just gets out the whole thing.
We've... we've, you know, we've pulled a discreet veil over the whole Jezoc debacle.
Because I've got my own show. I'll be telling you about it.
Something to do with... Right. Okay.
It's a genuine one I've come up with.

Song, right? Mama said, knock you out. I like to, like, you know, shadow box that. I've been working out today on the big bag, did a bit of boxing, because I'm in training. I challenged Camfield to a fight when I was pissed.
Thursday night, he was swaying. I challenged him to a fight. I offered him a thousand pounds prize money. That was the purse. Whether he won or lost, he still said no.
Well, he's a wuss. He's about fourteen or something.
Yeah, but he's about six foot.
Maybe he was scared of killing me. Jezoc is not scared of that.
Jezoc's gone. He's out of it.
There might be a comeback special one day, but thank God he's gone.
Yeah. I'm putting it out. I'm putting it out over the airs.
You know, like, you know, Death Row and Puffy and all that, and Tupac and all that. That's like me and Camfield.
I'm saying come and get it, Camfield. I'm saying I'm here, you know what I mean?
That East Coast-West Coast rivalry we can recreate amongst DJs.
Steve Lamacq, outside now! Have you seen him? He's a weedy little dweeb.
You can't actually say that, because, I mean, he's a nice nice guy.
Yeah, so you're going to fight Lamacq. I'm going to fight Camfield.
Let's keep it within XFM. Crowley.

Remember he had a fight once at school? And his defence, luckily he had a hymn book on him, and he hit the bloke in the nose with the hymn book. So you don't mess with Crowley, 'cause he's probably carrying, you know, Bibles, hymn books.
He's loaded. He's got some kind of religious paraphernalia with him.

Oh, imagine that. A little bit of papyrus across the eyelid. Ooh. You don't want to mess with Crowley. No, I'm saying, “Camfield, come and get it,” you know what I mean? He hangs out with his Deftones and all that lot.
Should we just ask out? Who should we threaten out? Who else can we threaten out?
Um, Well, let's, let's not go too mad.
Well, uh, what about Henry Rollins?
I've made a mistake. I've made an error there.
There are a lot of people I could have chosen. Jarvis, for instance. I've gone straight to...
A lot of people come before Henry Rowlands. Don't they?
Um, Some British heavyweight boxers, for example.
You know, I'd rather fight than hang out with Henry.

Um, before we carry on, before we, uh... 'cause I'm going to tell you about my, uh, my TV idea in a minute, Rick, 'cause this is an idea I've been working on. And it's serious. It's like, you know, Jezoc's got a certain strength, a certain quality.
Um, And I think you'll like this as well. But before we do that, I've been sent a a picture. A picture's been faxed through.
And it's a little challenge, as ever.
It's uh, make Ricky laugh. If you laugh at the picture I've got here, Rick, then uh, Martin in Crouch End,
He wins... uh, well, I thought we could give him...
I like it already, Martin in Crouch End.
I thought maybe we could give him the Baby Bird album.
Why? Why do you mean “we”? It's mine. You haven't got one, so you... go on then, yeah.
Well, I'll give that to him. But anyway, here's the picture.
I like it. There's a little explanation as well. And it's subtle, because I had to get right to the end for the big line. Anyway, You're not allowed to see this. No. Uh, That is fantastic.
So, well done to Martin. I think he wins an award.
Yeah, he does, yeah. Yeah, okay.
So if you want to win, um, something tasty, give us a... give us a call or fax us through a picture. 0171 580 1234. Your pictures, please. Make Ricky laugh.

Um, You know your idea of this new show, which I haven't heard yet, right? But we should start getting together all the other stuff or we're going to get ripped off. That one, I sounded just like Albert Tatlock, then, in the early 80s.

I love that fact that you you sort of... maybe you've got a sentence, he's got 15 words in. You reckon well, if I get if I get out an average of 5 coherent words to every 15 that I need to say in a sentence that would be enough.
Oh God. Right, Jam or Oasis?
Oh, no, come on. They're both good big bands aren't they.
All right, Gervais, next, let's talk about my my game, my TV idea.

Okay, let's do “All Around the World”, 'cause it's probably gonna be big all around the world, isn't it? Before that, the Jam, “All Around the World”. Um, got a fax here from my mate Nick. He's listening. Say hello to him.
Yeah. And, uh, apparently there's, he's found a great website about Joey Deacon. So we'll check that one out a little bit later.
We've had loads of ideas, haven't we, in the past?

And actually, I was wondering whether we should put out the phone number, 0171 580 2000. Um, the reason being that, A, you might perhaps want to... want us to perhaps, um, relate an old anecdote that you once heard on the show that you'd love to hear again.
Yeah. We could recreate the golden years.
We could recreate some of the classic moments from the Ricky Gervais Show.
And also, of course, we've had tens of thousands of ideas for products, for services, for TV shows especially, and uh, board games, all kinds of stuff.
I mean, the... we've come up with one recently, haven't we, that'll catch on. “Sleep with Me or Play with Lepers.”
I mean, that, that is a good service, isn't it?
It's an interesting show, that. Yeah. I imagine that's Channel 4.
Yeah, and we've also, of course, most famously perhaps had uh, the Penis Puppet Theatre.
Penis Puppet Theatre. So easy to manufacture. I don't know why publishers aren't, you know, knocking on my door.
A lot of other people are knocking on my door.
Get in the queue, mum. It's Ricky Gervais' Meat Rations.
All kinds of great games. Recreating.
Great games. And if you... I mean, if you've not ever heard us describing these, well, you've missed out.
The Teased Penguin's probably my greatest invention.
The Teased Penguin? Can you tell us again? I forget.
Well, it's just a penguin, right? You train, you put it in a lovely little French maid outfit, and it comes in, sort of breathes fishy breath on you, and slaps you on the face with its flipper.
But it doesn't let you go any further.
That's why it's the Tease Penguin.
I can see that on telly, myself.
Yeah, it's incredible. I don't know where you got the idea from.
I do, They just come into my head sometimes.
It's a great, it's a great show.
It's a, it's an exciting show, right?
All right? Crime has got so bad in the future... no, it's terrible... that, um, there's not enough hours in the day, right, for all the cases to be tried in court.
Because there's just not enough time. It's a bit like, you know, Judge Dredd sort of thing.
So what happens is, right, there's a night court, okay?
And it comes into session at 12 o'clock.
All right? And there's lots of lawyers and stuff, and they really deal with the dredge. I'm talking about the dredge, the crimes which you think are open and shut, Rick.
All right? The sort of stuff that Jezoc would just sort out, you know, with a bullet.
We're talking rapists and murderers and stuff.
Or people who just piss him off.
He's the hard-boiled, uh, lawyer, right? The, the, sort of, the main figure at night court.
And he gets dealt all these rough cases, right? And he thinks it's open and shut. Everyone thinks, oh, that person, he should be electrocuted or whatever.
But no. Ronnie sees something in them. He investigates the crime during the day, so he's only got, like, twelve hours to sort it out.
And then he presents the case at Night Court, right, at night. And maybe often... it's like Perry Mason meets, um, meets the...
So he wastes taxpayers' money investigating people that might be innocent?
That's, that's why Ronnie Midnight's much more loved.
But, uh, it's great, It would be great. Yeah. And it would start off with, like, dung, dung, dung, all rise, ju-ju-ju, for Night Court.
Maybe sort of set in the future.
Mm, not really. But, and, And, you know, who knows, Jezoc maybe could get, you know, he could, he could make a guest appearance. What do you think?
This rubbish about all this taxpayers' money investigating whether they're actually, you know...
They're innocent. You're more of a Jezok kind of guy.
Just shoot, shoot first. Don't even ask questions.
Don't, don't. Even, it's, If there's times, like, you know, of the essence, why ask questions? You've done, you know, what's the point?
You just like opening up old wounds, which is another favourite pastime of Jezoc, sometimes.
He loves opening up old wounds.
A great idea for maybe a board game or a TV show. Old wounds.
Oh, I'm going to work on this. Oh, and I've got Tip the Balance. I haven't even described that.
Emma goes out with a bloke in this.
It's a board game for four rugby players or more.
Yeah. Or the infirm. Or people who've just got no dignity left, and we can get 'em on screen doing that. This is, uh, “My Weakness Is None of”... dot dot dot. Obviously ran out of...
I was, uh, reading the News of the World on the way here, and, um, I didn't know this.
You know, um, uh, Tony Blair?
Cherie Blair. Um, his father-in-law, which is Cherie's dad, is that bloke out of Till Death Us Do Part.
Something about his... I don't know, I should get this right, really, 'cause it could be libellous, but it's something to do with some sort of dole cheat or something like that.
Cherie Blair's dad's a dole cheat?

Or he's claiming some sort of benefit fraud, I don't know. But he was always the same when he was living with his dad, Alf. He was married to Una Stubbs, wasn't he? That means Cherie Blair's mum is Una Stubbs.
I'll stop you there, Rick. I'll stop you there.
It's fiction. I've tried to explain this to you before, haven't I? The stuff on the TV,
A lot of it is real.
Some of it's fake. They're not really those people. Understand? EastEnders, for instance, that's not real. That's not real people.
Uh, yeah. Well, obviously you're embarrassed, 'cause obviously that is real, 'cause I've seen 'em in real life. They were at Phoenix, got 'em playing football. So that is real.
No, that was the actor, that was the actors.
Mm. Phil Mitchell was there, and Ricky Butcher.
That was the actors. I've, We have been through this before. We've, Because I went through this the same day that I explained to you that it, only in the cat world can you piss on an object.
I've got a new stereo that way.
They said, “Get out of the shop,” but it was too late. I've got a new stereo. And it doesn't, it sort of... it shorts out, 'cause I actually weed in one of the back of the speakers.
But it's mine, I've gotta get that. Jeff.
Buckley. Everybody here wants you. Wow. Nearly end of the, uh... the Nearly of the show with it, innit?
I can't even be bothered to criticise your...
It's not worth it, is it?
So late in the day, if you... I mean, you're not gonna master it at the age of, what, 45, however old you are. You know, I mentioned, um, I guess we could call it Freak Show or something like that.
Where celebrities with deformities come on...
Suck the most deformed. What would you put forward as your most deformed bit?
Well, luckily, um, uh, sucking my most deformed bit would be curiously enjoyable for me.
Anyway, uh, I asked for a few more celebrities who've got deformities and various people have called in. Uh, Jez in East Barnet mentioned John Thaw, who, of course...
Well, John's left leg, I think, is shorter than his right. He always sort of hobbles a bit as he walks.
